hypotheses.description: The synthetic intervention's effect on viability in cell-a is attributable to incomplete perturbation of SYNTHETIC_TARGET, such that residual target activity sustains the phenotype.
The synthetic intervention's effect on viability in cell-a is attributable to multi-target activity, such that engagement of targets beyond SYNTHETIC_TARGET contributes to the phenotype.

differing_assumptions: Hypothesis a assumes the intervention engages SYNTHETIC_TARGET but does not fully suppress its activity, whereas hypothesis b assumes the intervention engages additional targets beyond SYNTHETIC_TARGET.
Hypothesis a treats the observed phenotype as a consequence of residual SYNTHETIC_TARGET function, whereas hypothesis b treats it as a consequence of combined target engagement.
Hypothesis a predicts that increasing target engagement would alter the phenotype, whereas hypothesis b predicts that eliminating off-target engagement would alter the phenotype.
interpretation_boundaries: The planned flat synthetic assay is an engineering fixture and cannot establish any biological mechanism, regulatory edge, or causal effect.
The planned result cannot distinguish whether any observed response is due to incomplete perturbation, multi-target activity, or any other biological process.
No measurement, biological mechanism, or efficacy is established by this fixture; the independent execution gate may override or refuse the proposed action.
